transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hi Mr. Park, come on in. Please have a seat.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Now, before we go over your discharge papers and your recovery, I need to discuss something that happened while you were in the hospital. We made a mistake with your care.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A mistake? What do you mean?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: When you were admitted, we took an ECG, which is the heart rhythm test. The machine flagged an abnormal result immediately, but I didn't review that result for four hours. Because I missed that flag, there was a delay in diagnosing your cardiac event and starting your treatment. Does that make sense so far?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh. I... I didn't know that. I just thought I was waiting for the doctors to decide what to do. Was it... was it dangerous?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It did delay the process by four hours. I am sorry. This was my responsibility, and I apologize for failing to check the results promptly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I guess I just felt really scared when I was lying there and no one was coming in. I didn't know if I was doing something wrong or if—

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right, but the important thing is that the treatment eventually started and your vitals stabilized.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I mean, I just didn't have anyone there with me. My parents are back home and I didn't know who to ask for help. I felt like I was just...

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. Now, looking at the chart, the delayed intervention didn't result in long-term damage, but it wasn't the standard of care you should have received. Do you understand why the delay happened?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yeah, you didn't look at the machine. I just... I'm kind of shaking. I don't really know what this means for my health now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Everything is stable now. Look, I actually have to go see another patient in a few minutes, so let's wrap this up quickly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Wait, I have a question about the medication. If the diagnosis was late, does that mean the medicine is—

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The medication is the same regardless of the four-hour window.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just feel like I'm not really sure what to do if it happens again. Like, what are my rights if this happens again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You're fine now. We'll just keep an eye on things.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But how? Do I need more tests? Do I need to go back sooner?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll see how you feel over the next week.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So there's no specific plan?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Just stay tuned for an email from the clinic about your next follow-up.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't really know when that will be.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It should come eventually. I really have to run now. Have a good afternoon, Mr. Park.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('wrap this up quickly', 'have to go see another patient', 'really have to run now').

E.justification: Error named in first two turns, used lay language, checked comprehension twice ('Does that make sense so far?', 'Do you understand why the delay happened?'), and avoided false reassurance regarding the error itself.

A.justification: Resident used direct apology language ('I am sorry', 'I apologize') and explicitly took personal responsibility ('This was my responsibility').

R.justification: Patient's emotional bids regarding fear and isolation were consistently met with factual redirection ('Right, but the important thing is...', 'Everything is stable now').

T.justification: Resident provided only placeholders ('we'll see', 'stay tuned', 'should come eventually') with no specific timeline or patient role.
